posts.title: The Stupefaction of Experts
posts.description: Several serious topics this month. The fear surrounding AI is, I argue, a lever for politics and profit, and it distracts from simpler questions: who owns the machine, and who answers for it? I also look at how the technology moves power away from experts, and at the quiet isolation it brings to some of the smartest people I know. posts.title: The Future I Want Runs on Salt
posts.description: A mixed bag this month. Some thoughts on living with imperfect technology, a small rant about how people choose to share what they've learned, and an essay on incentives that made me rethink some of my own views. Then some brain food, both good and worrying, and a piece of battery news that makes me look forward to the future. 🔋

posts.title: Things That Happened Quietly
posts.description: A vacation month, mostly away from LLM news. I read a book on negotiation that turned out to be about listening, and thought about how conversations flow (or don't) inside organizations. I also noticed a few developments that got less attention than they deserved: in classrooms, at home, and in the oil markets. To close, a short text on what it takes for a community to exist at all. 🫐
